newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-HOWLEY OUT OF LIONS TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HOWLEY OUT OF LIONS TOUR.

text.p: Welsh scrum-half Rob Howley dislocated his left shoulder during the Lions' emphatic 42-12 victory over Natal at Kings Park on Saturday and will miss the rest of the South African tour.
Howley, regarded as a certain selection for next week's first test in Cape Town, and Lions manager Fran Cotton could not hide his disappointment.

"Rob dislocated the AC-joint in his left shoulder early on in the match and he will need an operation. He'll be returning home as soon as the medical officer rules that he is fit to travel. We'll consider his replacement tonight," said Cotton.
"There was nothing intentional about the incident - it was the sort of accident that can happen in a match situation.

"Obviously it's very disappointing for Rob and also for the entire team. He's a world-class player. But it doesn't deflect one inch from our aim which is to win the test series against the Springboks.

"We picked scrum-halves who play in the same way as Howley and that could turn out to be a bonus. Maybe they're not in the same league but they'll slot in easily enough," Lions coach Ian McGeechan said.
Cotton said Howley's replacement would be announced on Sunday. The leading contenders would appear to be fellow Welshman Paul John and England's Kyran Bracken.
